claims.text: High-temperature wear resistance of FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coatings is governed by their ability to maintain microstructural integrity under mechanical stress.
Suppressing grain-boundary sliding improves the high-temperature wear resistance of FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coatings.
The material is a FeNiCrCoCu thin protective coating deposited on conventional metals.
The proposed test varies temperature from 25 to 800 °C.
The proposed test uses nanoindentation depths from 100 to 500 nm.
The proposed test uses loading rates from 1 to 10 mN/s.
Temperature and indentation loading produce microstructural evolution involving grain size, grain-boundary morphology, and dislocation density.
Grain-boundary sliding in the coating is thermally activated.
Grain-boundary sliding and dislocation glide are influenced by coating composition, grain size, and indentation-induced stress.
Wear resistance increases with temperature up to an unspecified critical temperature.
Above the critical temperature, grain-boundary sliding and dislocation glide cause wear resistance to decrease.
Room-temperature wear behavior is the baseline against which the high-temperature response is compared.
Failure to observe either a post-critical-temperature decrease in wear resistance or evidence of grain-boundary sliding and dislocation glide would falsify the hypothesis.
